note: Hebrew niqqudim are small cakes or biscuits (perhaps crumbly or speckled); "cracknels" is an obscure English term.
Hebrew 'asherim are wooden cult objects of the goddess Asherah, not groves of trees; the KJV followed the Septuagint/Vulgate "grove." Same at 14:23, 15:13, 16:33.
Hebrew matsevot are standing stones erected as cult markers, not carved images.
Hebrew qadesh means "consecrated one," a male functionary attached to a shrine (traditionally a cult prostitute); "sodomites" imports a reference to Sodom that the Hebrew lacks. Same at 15:12.
